fact.claim: If you have access to an existing private CA created by AWS Private CA, ACM can request a private certificate from it; the CA can be in your account or shared with you by a different account.
fact.question: What do you need before ACM can issue a private certificate?

values.display: shared with you by a different account

evidence.quote: If you have access to an existing private CA created by AWS Private CA, AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) can request a certificate suited for use in your private key infrastructure (PKI). The CA may either reside in your account or be shared with you by a different account.
evidence.title: Private certificates in AWS Certificate Manager

fact.author: mine-07-behavior+decisions

votes.reason: The quote gives a sufficient condition ('If you have access to an existing private CA ... ACM can request a certificate'), not 'only if'; the CA in your account or shared by another account is supported.
The private certificates page says ACM can request a certificate if you have access to an existing private CA created by AWS Private CA, in your account or shared by a different account.
